items.new_text: The `regra_prioridade` engine now evaluates active rules when a conversation enters a queue (`dominio/entrada.ts`, `dominio/fluxo.ts`), and the first match sets `conversa.prioridade`. Earlier `regras-prioridade.ts` implemented only CRUD. Pipe still has no explicit order column: queue-scoped rules precede tenant-scoped rules, as in SLA `escolherRegra` in `sla.ts`; within a scope, older `criado_em` wins. Add an `ordem` column only if reordering without recreation becomes necessary. An empty condition matches all conversations IN SCOPE: `regra_prioridade.condicao` defaults to `{}` (`packages/db/src/schema/gestao.ts`), and scope already filters applicability. This deliberately differs from empty `regra_fila` conditions, which never match because their conditions are the whole rule.
Deterministic evaluation order: `fila` scope (0) before `tenant` (1), then older creation time, then ID for exact ties.
Fields offered by a newly arrived conversation, shaped like `ContextoDaConversa` in `regra-fila.ts`.

Return the first active rule whose scope and condition match, checking cheap scope first. `null` leaves `conversa.prioridade` at default `sem_prioridade`, preserving behavior without registered rules.
Evaluate rules in deterministic order: ties in `ordem` break by ID, as in distribution spec §7. Without that tie-break, two order-0 rules depend on unspecified PostgreSQL row order.

Return the first matching active rule, or `null` to use the inbox default queue. An active rule with no conditions never matches because `avaliarExpressao` returns false for an empty list; otherwise an accidentally empty rule would capture every conversation before rules below it.

Report unreachable rule indexes: an active rule without conditions never matches, and a rule below an identical one never wins. Show these configuration errors so a manager understands why a newly tested rule has no effect.

Inbound rules (metrics spec §8) choose a conversation's arrival queue. Unlike unspecified Blip documentation, Pipe evaluates in displayed order, with FIRST match winning, and combines each rule's conditions by user-chosen AND or OR. If none matches, `inbox.fila_padrao_id` selects the default queue outside this module. Keep this module pure for the `'use client'` form; importing Drizzle or `@pipe/db` would pull `pg` into the browser. Delegate expression evaluation to `@pipe/core` (`score/motor.ts`) so operators, accent/case normalization and dotted paths have one definition.
`mensagem` is the customer's first message; other fields come from the contact. `contato.atributos.` is a PREFIX followed by the tenant-defined extra-field key, e.g. `contato.atributos.plano`.
Accept one of four fixed fields or an extra field with a nonempty key. A mistyped arbitrary field would make a rule silently never match and send conversations to the wrong queue.

Share contact-name rules between router and flow because Blip uses the SAME creation template for both. Source name step module 96904 changes only labels through three `ng-if="$ctrl.template != 'master'"`; `required`, 2–30 length, file `accept` and per-key sanitization are identical. Server `validateApplicationName` runs through `prepareApplicationData` for every template. Evidence: source `portal.js` 25.204.0-v0.43.1 modules `CreateApplicationController` (18502), name template (96904), and `CreateApplicationService.validateApplicationName`. Keep the rules outside either screen and enforce them both in browser validation and the Server Action against direct POSTs.

Require a LETTER first. Source `validateApplicationName` uses `/(^[a-zA-Z])/` because `shortName = name.toLowerCase()` becomes the platform contact identifier; a digit or `(` cannot start that address.
Apply the source's per-keystroke name sanitization.

Source `application.shortName = application.name.toLowerCase()` would leave spaces (e.g. 'Meu Fluxo' to `meu fluxo`), though observed real short names have none; an unseen downstream service likely normalizes them. Pipe replaces spaces with hyphens before saving `fluxo.short_name` (migration `0020`) so addresses work. Do not add a unique index: existing name uniqueness is checked by Server Action `select` over `nome`, and an index here would newly make 'Meu Bot' collide with 'meu-bot'.
`conferir` returns one of two screen-supplied sentences. Source `errorMsg.invalidName` says 'fluxo' while the router screen says 'roteador'; the rule stays identical and only the noun changes.

Validate names in source order: form `validApplicationFormErrors` checks required/min/max length before service `validateApplicationName` checks the first letter. Return the FIRST refusal, as source `checkFormValidity` stops at the first invalid field.

Source name-step `<upload-button>` (module 96904) accepts literal `accept="'.gif, .png, .jpeg, .jpg'"` and `ng-mime-type="image/png, image/jpg, image/jpeg, image/gif"`. `.jpg` and `.jpeg` share `image/jpeg`, so four extensions mean three real MIME types. Pipe's `maxBytes` has no source counterpart: Blip stores a media URL, while Pipe stores a data URI in the row (`acoes.ts`), so a 256 KB file expands to about 350 KB base64 while remaining adequate for a 150px avatar.

Check file signatures in bytes, NEVER client extension or `Content-Type`. The canonical 15-format table is `packages/armazenamento/src/tipo-real.ts`; duplicate only these three signatures here because importing its built package into Next would add a build dependency. If more formats are accepted, use `tipoReal` from `@pipe/armazenamento`.
MIME determined from bytes, or `null` if none of the three signatures match.

Blip sanitizes on EVERY keystroke with `ng-change` and `validateSpecialCharacter`. Its allowed class `a-zA-Z0-9[]()_ -` excludes accents, silently turning 'Fluxo Padrão' into 'Fluxo Padro'. Pipe retains filtering to protect `shortName` (`nomeCurto`) but adds Portuguese accented letters; reproducing the source bug is unnecessary.

`regra_prioridade` CRUD was added to complete REST without a new `apps/gestao-vite` page. Historically there was no engine: `conversa.prioridade` was set elsewhere, and the CRUD task asked only to store configuration. The later `prioridade-motor.ts` (`avaliarPrioridade`/`carregarRegrasDePrioridadeAtivas`) now evaluates it in `dominio/entrada.ts`/`dominio/fluxo.ts` on queue entry. Historical no-order decision also followed a schema without an order column (`packages/db/src/schema/gestao.ts`) and no consumer; current deterministic order is queue scope before tenant, then `criado_em` (see motor). Retain these historical reasons rather than suggesting the engine is still absent. Accept only `tenant`/`fila` in `escopoTipo`, following SLA; unsupported `inbox`/`equipe`/`etiqueta` scopes must not be stored as silently ineffective rules.
Require a plain object for rule conditions, not an array or scalar; `jsonb` accepts any JSON but a rule condition must map criteria.
Validate the alert after both final deadline values: a PATCH may change only
one deadline while retaining the other.
Reject a deadline shortened below an existing alert rather than storing an alert that can never fire.
`sla_conversa.regra_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`: deleting the rule would
silently delete timers for conversations still running under it.
Cap at one week; larger deadlines are likely unit mistakes, such as seconds entered as minutes.

Write `regra_sla` here while `configuracoes.ts` `carregarRegras` reads rules and joins queue names for `regras/sla`. Follow `cadastros.ts` REST `ErroPipe` statuses. Keep SLA separate from queue, pause and inbound-rule registration, as `comunicacao.ts` is separate. Reuse `regra.gerenciar` from `gravarRegraFila`; catalog label 'Gerenciar regras de fila, prioridade e SLA' already covers it. Pipe accepts only `tenant` and `fila` `escopoTipo`: database `ESCOPOS_REGRA` also allows `inbox`, `equipe` and `etiqueta`, but SLA motor `escolherRegra` in `dominio/gestao/sla.ts` cannot apply those; reject them rather than saving inert rules.
Missing or `null` means no alert; a supplied alert must fire BEFORE the deadline.

Satisfaction report, metrics spec §6. Store scale with every score in `resposta_pesquisa` (`escala_min`, `escala_max`): CSAT 4 on 1–5 and NPS 4 on 0–10 differ and must not share a chart. Group by both type AND scale so mixed scales cannot enter the same mean. Response-rate numerator and denominator both use conversations closed in the selected period; different populations would yield a meaningless rate.
One pair per survey; group mean is sum divided by sum, never mean of means.
Order CSAT before NPS and smaller scales before larger ones for a
stable report every time.
Share of the bar; a division of counts rather than a spec metric.
Surveys generated for conversations closed in the period, answered or not.
Responses divided by conversations closed in the period, shown alongside the mean.
Response-rate denominator: conversations closed in the period.
Cap comments because this is a recent sample, not a full survey export.

Read stored classes from best to worst. `classe` has different vocabulary for CSAT (`satisfeito`/`insatisfeito`) and NPS (`promotor`/`neutro`/`detrator`). Show stored classification without recomputing historical scores, which could introduce new thresholds.
The transaction already has the tenant fixed; `consultar` only names the block, as in Management.
Run serially, never in parallel: `Promise.all` inside the transaction can
silently clear `pipe.tenant_id`.
Return this account's live router or 404; a non-router flow is an invalid request.
Normalize the form so hidden fields are not stored.

Router services mirror Blip `master.services` (`referencias-blip/pesquisa/blip-servicos-do-roteador.md`) in `roteador_servico` (migration 0024). Follow `ciclo-de-vida-do-fluxo.ts`/Chatwoot `inboxes_controller`: find router within account (404 otherwise), authorize, validate, write and audit. Source form requires unique router-local service name as `Redirect.address`, one live non-router account flow per service, at most one principal bot, hidden persistence/expiry for principal, and hidden expiry for persistent; expiry is required otherwise. Pipe defines integer expiry in MINUTES from 1 to 525,600 (source help says seconds but UI does not show a unit), 60-character name, 409 instead of silently replacing an existing principal, and deletion of principal without auto-promotion; conversations then fall back to the queue. All writes require `automacao.fluxo.editar` because changing a service edits its router.
Return this router's association or 404.

Source `PermissionsList.html` has no master-service row: 'Serviços' comes from `getTemplateSetupItem()`, not menu catalog. Use its nearest `basicConfigurations` permission for the contact itself; existing account-level editors retain access (migration 0035).
Change supplied fields only, then validate the result with creation rules.

Source `PermissionsList.html` has no master-service row: 'Serviços' comes from `getTemplateSetupItem()`, not menu catalog. Use its nearest `basicConfigurations` permission for the contact itself; existing account-level editors retain access (migration 0035).
Remove the router service but keep its chatbot. On the next message, conversations at its former position return to the principal service because that position no longer resolves.

Source `PermissionsList.html` has no master-service row: 'Serviços' comes from `getTemplateSetupItem()`, not menu catalog. Use its nearest `basicConfigurations` permission for the contact itself; existing account-level editors retain access (migration 0035).
Router associations with their chatbots, principal first.
`GET …/servicos`: `null` when the flow is outside this account (404). A non-router flow returns an empty result and the screen shows 'não encontrado'.
For one rule and conversation, choose new state and emit alert or breach at most once each.
Strict idempotence: a terminal row never changes again, even if a sweep
revisits the same conversation a month later.

SLA clock activates the existing `regra_sla`/`sla_conversa` storage. Like media-download scheduling in `../../filas.ts` (`agendarVarreduraDownloadMidia`/`relogioMidia`), BullMQ `pipe-sla` nudges a periodic sweep, with an in-memory dev/test path. `sla_conversa` is authoritative; a lost job only delays processing until the next sweep. Pipe does NOT pause outside business hours: neither `referencias-blip/pesquisa/regras-blip.md` nor `blip-desk-regras-tecnicas.md` documents Blip doing so; the observed first-response timer RESET after an agent reply is different. Existing `dominio/gestao/sla.ts` records the same gap. Pass `horario: null` to `avaliarSla` for 24/7 evaluation; it already accepts a queue schedule if later evidence warrants one. Freeze the clock when a conversation closes, so the next sweep cannot breach one closed before its deadline. Choose one winning rule PER TARGET, not one per conversation: `sla_conversa` uniqueness `(conversa_id, regra_id)` permits concurrent first-response and resolution rules. Apply queue-scope precedence over tenant for each target, as more specific manager configuration.
For `resposta` (`tempo_resposta`), count only while the customer's message
is last. Once the agent or bot answers, this target has no remaining start time.
